text:
Buffalo has handed Zach Benson a top-line job, and he has run with it. He's playing 20:12 a night, up from 15:53 last season, and on the ice for 72% of the Sabres' power-play chances. The Athletic's "16 NHL stats" piece put it in a headline: "Zach Benson has arrived as a star."

The goals haven't followed yet. He has 3 on 8.5 expected goals (the quality of his chances), a 5.7% shooting rate against a league norm of 13.4%. Our numbers flag him as due: he keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances. The assists, 14 of them, have run the other way, helped by teammates who've scored 7.3 more goals than expected with him on the ice.

The play-driving is not luck. Buffalo owns 56.4% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey rated his impact on his team's chances in the 98th percentile of forwards last season. For a 21-year-old on a struggling team, that's the part to watch, along with how the goal and assist luck trade places.
